描述_EN: by the tang dynasty (618-906 ad), from which this textile dates, there were a thousand caves decorated with religious scenes. this shrine site is one of china’s great buddhist pilgrimage complexes and is situated near the oasis town of dunhuang. the site is part of an area of central asia now called the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia, from china to europe. the insides of each cave-shrine were painted with coloured murals, some of which survive to this day. camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed the goods from oasis to oasis. this textile was brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862-1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas – while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. it was recovered from cave 17 of the mogao grottoes. the shrines were carved out of the gravel conglomerate naturally occurring in the region.
描述_ZN: 到了唐代（公元618-906年），也就是这幅纺织品的年代，有一千个洞穴被装饰有宗教场景。 该圣地是中国伟大的佛教朝圣地之一，位于敦煌绿洲镇附近。 该遗址是中亚地区的一部分，现在被称为丝绸之路，是一系列从中国到欧洲横跨亚洲的陆上贸易路线。 每个洞窟神龛的内部都绘有彩色壁画，其中有些壁画至今仍在。 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递货物。 年，这个纺织品被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：丝绸之路对思想交流也很重要--当丝绸纺织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 是在莫高窟第17窟发现的。 这些神龛是由该地区自然形成的砾石砾石雕刻而成的。
